newsitem.title: USA: Stockton,Calif.,debates bonds for Christian school.
newsitem.headline: Stockton,Calif.,debates bonds for Christian school.

text.p: A private Christian school's bid for tax-exempt bond funds has fanned a political storm in this northern California town.

United Christian Schools Inc asked the Stockton City Council to approve an $8.9 million tax-exempt bond issue so it could refinance its existing mortgages and build a new preschool and high school in the city, located about 60 miles east of San Francisco.
The city council was poised to vote on the proposal in late January but questions about the separation of church and state were raised, prompting the council to delay any action.

"Prudence dictates a careful and public discussion of the justification for a municipality to issue tax-exempt bonds for the construction of private sectarian schools," state Senator Patrick Johnston said in a January 27 letter to Stockton's mayor, requesting postponement of the proposed issuance.
The city council is now expected to consider the bond issue at its meeting on February 24.
United Christian Schools Inc said it was surprised by the controversy over its bond proposal.
"There's a lot of misinformation," Dennis Gibson, superintendent of United Christian Schools said.
He said United Christian Schools is not a church and that its schools are open to students of all faiths.
"We do have religious studies. But we're not catering to any particular faith," Gibson said.
If the city council approves the bond issue, the bonds would be repaid with revenues generated at United Christian Schools Inc's six schools in Stockton.
"It (the bond issue) wouldn't cost the city anything," Gibson said.
